scores.evidence: Merges are commutative and idempotent, offline editing comes for free, and the library is mature.
scores.rationale: Claims about Yjs/CRDT semantics, idempotent resends, relative positions, UndoManager scoping and the real tombstone/memory overheads of CRDTs are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: A browser-based editor where many people edit the same rich-text document at once. It shows live cursors and presence, keeps working offline
scores.rationale: Covers every implied core capability (co-editing, presence, offline, history, comments, sharing), is credibly buildable by a small team, and every exclusion is explicit with a pull-forward trigger.

scores.evidence: One process owns each doc, assigned by consistent hash on doc ID. The doc lives in memory on one node
scores.rationale: Data ownership (content AP in the update log, metadata CP in Postgres), per-doc routing, and identity/authz are applied consistently across all phases with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: 10k fuzz sessions with zero divergence. A `kill -9` on the collab node mid-edit loses zero acked updates.
scores.rationale: The riskiest assumption (convergence) is fuzz-tested in Phase 1 before features, every phase has checkable exit criteria, and a production divergence detector continues validation after launch.

scores.evidence: Switch to OT (ShareDB-style, server-ordered) if CRDT tombstone or memory overhead goes over budget (for example, more than 50 MB
scores.rationale: Numbers are hedged as estimates ('about 200', 'about 50 ms') and every default decision states the condition that would overturn it and how it would be observed.

scores.evidence: clients report a doc state hash periodically, the server compares, and a divergence counter has an alert at zero tolerance.
scores.rationale: Covers the domain's hardest failures—silent divergence, lost acked edits, bad snapshots, revoked-while-offline edits, detached anchors, paste XSS, memory DoS, duplicates—each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: On deploy, a node flushes its docs and hands them off before shutting down.
scores.rationale: Deploy/rollback, migrations, drain-and-handoff, meaningful alerts and SLO burn rates are concrete and sized to a small team, but incident ownership and on-call/runbook response are never assigned.

scores.evidence: Use WebRTC peer-to-peer for presence only, if server egress cost for presence dominates.
scores.rationale: Some cost drivers (egress, storage growth, build-vs-buy) and controls (compaction, S3 trigger, load shedding) appear, but there are no estimates, ranges, or reasoning about how run cost grows with usage.

scores.evidence: Concurrency algorithm (most irreversible: it fixes the stored data format)
scores.rationale: Explicitly ranks the irreversible decisions (stored format, add-only schema), validates them earliest, defers lock-ins like multi-region and microservices, and names exit paths (OT, hosted backend).

scores.evidence: Modular monolith: one repo, one codebase, two process types. ... They are split because they scale differently, not for organizational reasons.
scores.rationale: Starts with a textarea-plus-Y.Text slice, Postgres-for-everything, single region, and defers every heavier component behind a stated trigger; nothing essential is cut.

scores.evidence: A logged-in user opens `/d/:docId` and types "hello". A second browser, signed in as a different user, sees "hello" appear.
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: dependency-justified phase order, named libraries and table schemas, checkable exit criteria per phase, and revisit triggers that say how to change course.

checklist.evidence: CRDT using Yjs. Merges are commutative and idempotent, offline editing comes for free, and the library is mature.
A versioned ProseMirror/TipTap schema, add-only: node and mark types are never removed or renamed.
N simulated clients make random concurrent edits under partition, reordering and duplication.
Each update is appended to the Postgres update log before the ack. ... Never delete log entries until the snapshot is verified.
One process owns each doc, assigned by consistent hash on doc ID. ... Client reconnect with exponential backoff and jitter.
Two devices that each edit offline for 24 hours merge correctly.
the JWT and role are checked when the WebSocket connects, and on every message. ... the server closes or downgrades active sockets within 5 seconds.
Per-user undo with Y.UndoManager, tracking local edits only. ... A restore is applied as a new forward update; the log is never rewritten.
It is ephemeral (never persisted), throttled to about 50 ms, and capped in size. ... no awareness data reaches doc_updates.
plain text in a <textarea> bound to a Y.Text ... Rich text depends on proven sync, so it waits.
Max update size of 1 MB ... above N editors, cursor fidelity is dropped. ... Hot docs go read-only for overflow viewers.
Clients below the minimum schema version are forced to reload. ... A schema v1→v2 migration passes against an anonymized copy of the snapshot corpus.

traps.evidence: CRDT using Yjs. Merges are commutative and idempotent
Buy or adopt: Yjs, y-protocols, TipTap/ProseMirror
Rich text depends on proven sync, so it waits.
Never ack before the write is durable.
The server still relays, stores and authorizes.

note: An exemplary plan—correct CRDT/durability semantics, sync proven first, thorough domain failure coverage, explicit reversibility reasoning—weak only on money-cost estimation and incident ownership.
